title: Why Hockey Matters
intro_es: Entender el hockey es entender a tus vecinos y compañeros: aquí tienes lo esencial.
paragraphs: If you live in Edmonton, you can't escape hockey. In winter, you will see kids carrying hockey bags almost as big as they are, neighbours flooding their backyards to make ice rinks and coworkers wearing team jerseys on game days. Hockey is officially Canada's national winter sport, but for many people it is more than a sport: it is part of their identity.

Why is hockey so important? Part of the answer is the climate. For generations, Canadians spent long winters on frozen lakes, ponds and outdoor rinks. Hockey was something you could play almost anywhere there was ice. Many adults have childhood memories of early morning practices, cold arenas and parents drinking coffee in the stands. Today, many neighbourhoods in Edmonton have a community rink.

Edmonton has a professional team with a long history, and the city gets very excited when the team does well. During the playoffs, the elimination rounds in spring, the mood in the city changes. Restaurants are full, cars have small flags and some fans stop shaving until their team is eliminated. This tradition is called a playoff beard.

You don't need to understand every rule to enjoy a game. Here are the basics: two teams of six players, including a goalie, try to shoot a small rubber disc, the puck, into the other team's net. A game has three periods of twenty minutes. When a player breaks a rule, they go to the penalty box, and the other team gets a power play, a chance to score with an extra player on the ice.

Watching a game with coworkers is a great way to connect. If someone invites you to a bar or a house to watch, say yes! Ask simple questions like “Who's their best player?” or “Why did the referee stop the game?” People love explaining hockey to newcomers. On Monday, you can ask, “Did you catch the game?” and start a conversation easily.
Maybe you will become a big fan, or maybe you will prefer soccer forever. Either way, understanding hockey helps you understand your new neighbours.

the rows of seats where people sit to watch a game

options: Hockey is a difficult sport that only Canadians can understand.
Edmonton's team wins the playoffs almost every year.
Hockey is a big part of Canadian identity, and watching it with others helps you connect.
main_idea.why_es: El texto explica por qué el hockey es parte de la identidad canadiense y cómo usarlo para conectar.

questions.q: Why did hockey become so popular in Canada?
options: Because the government built arenas in every city
Because long winters gave people ice almost everywhere
Because it was the only sport on television
questions.why_es: Los inviernos largos daban hielo en lagos, estanques y pistas al aire libre: se podía jugar casi en todas partes.

options: When fans don't shave until their team is eliminated
A beard that players must have to play in the playoffs
A prize for the best player of the season
questions.why_es: Algunos aficionados dejan de rasurarse durante la liguilla hasta que su equipo queda eliminado.

questions.q: What happens during a power play?
options: The game stops for twenty minutes.
One team has an extra player because of a penalty.
questions.why_es: Cuando un jugador va a la banca de castigo, el otro equipo juega con un jugador más.

questions.q: According to the text, what is a good question when you watch with coworkers?
options: How much money do the players earn?
questions.why_es: El texto sugiere preguntas sencillas como Who's their best player?, porque a la gente le gusta explicar.
